elements.char: Dataset Split
elements.label: formula

elements.char: Each volume is randomly assigned to one of the following six component datasets: training, valida-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tion, multi-coil test, single-coil test, multi-coil challenge, or single-coil challenge. Table 4 shows the
elements.label: text

elements.char: number of volumes assigned to each dataset. The training and validation datasets may be used to
elements.label: text

elements.char: fit model parameters or to determine hyperparameter values. The test dataset is used to compare
elements.label: text

elements.char: the results across different approaches.
elements.label: text

elements.char: To ensure that models do not overfit to the test set, the
elements.label: text

elements.char: ground truth reconstructions are not publicly released for this set.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Evaluation on the test set is
elements.label: text

elements.char: accomplished by uploading results to the public leaderboard at http://fastmri.org/. The challenge
elements.label: text

elements.char: portion of the dataset will be forthcoming.
elements.label: text

elements.char: A volume from the train or validation dataset is used in both the single-coil and multi-coil
elements.label: text

elements.char: tracks, whereas a volume from the test or challenge dataset is only used in either the single-coil
elements.label: text

elements.char: or the multi-coil track.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Volumes were only included in a single test or challenge set to ensure
elements.label: text

elements.char: information from one could not be used to help the result in another.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Cartesian Undersampling
elements.label: formula

elements.char: Volumes in the test and challenge datasets contain undersampled k-space data. The undersampling
elements.label: text

elements.char: is performed by retrospectively masking k-space lines from a fully-sampled acquisition. k-space lines
elements.label: text

elements.char: are omitted only in the phase encoding direction, so as to simulate physically realizable accelerations
elements.label: text

elements.char: in 2D data acquisitions. The same undersampling mask is applied to all slices in a volume, with
elements.label: text

elements.char: each case consisting of a single volume. The overall acceleration factor is set randomly to either four
elements.label: text

elements.char: or eight (representing a four-fold or an eight-fold acceleration, respectively), with equal probability
elements.label: text

elements.char: for each.
elements.label: text

elements.char: All undersampling masks are generated by first including some number of adjacent lowest-
elements.label: text

elements.char: frequency k-space lines to provide a fully-sampled k-space region.
elements.label: text

elements.char: When the acceleration factor
elements.label: text

elements.char: equals four, the fully-sampled central region includes 8% of all k-space lines; when it equals eight,
elements.label: text

elements.char: 4% of all k-space lines are included. The remaining k-space lines are included differently for both
elements.label: text

elements.char: knee and brain cases. For knee, the remaining k-space lines are included uniformly at random, with
elements.label: text

elements.char: the probability set so that, on average, the undersampling mask achieves the desired acceleration
elements.label: text

elements.char: factor.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Random undersampling is chosen in order to meet the general conditions for compressed
elements.label: text

elements.char: sensing [2, 23], for a fair comparison of learned reconstruction algorithms with traditional sparsity-
elements.label: text

elements.char: based regularizers. For brain, after a random offset from the start, the remaining lines are sampled
elements.label: text

elements.char: equidistant from each other with a spacing that achieves the desired acceleration factor. Equidistant
elements.label: text

elements.char: was chosen because of ease of implementation on existing MRI machines. Figure
elements.label: text

elements.char: 5 depicts the k-
elements.label: text

elements.char: space trajectories for random and equidistant undersampling at four and eight acceleration factors.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Metrics
elements.label: formula

elements.char: The assessment of MRI reconstruction quality is of paramount relevance to develop and compare
elements.label: text

elements.char: machine learning and medical imaging systems [51, 53, 3, 58]. The most commonly used evaluation
elements.label: text

elements.char: metrics in the MRI reconstruction literature [3] include (normalized) mean squared error, which
elements.label: text

elements.char: measures pixel-wise intensity differences between reconstructed and reference images, and signal-
elements.label: text

elements.char: to-noise ratio, which measures the degree to which image information rises above background noise.
elements.label: text

elements.char: These metrics are appealing because they are easy to understand and efficient to compute. However,
elements.label: text

elements.char: they both evaluate pixels independently, ignoring the overall image structure.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Additional metrics have been introduced in the literature to capture structural distortion [41, 6,
elements.label: text

elements.char: 58]. For example, the structural similarity index [53] and its extended version, multiscale structural
